alloy.preparation: Experimental alloy melted in a 500-lb vacuum furnace, hot-rolled to 0.5-in plate, cold-rolled to 0.25-in plate; solution-annealed 2000°F (1092°C) for 60 min and quenched in flowing water. Cylindrical specimens 0.25-in diameter × 0.75-in length, polished to 600-grit SiC and mounted in Teflon compression gasket; ultrasonically degreased, pickled in 25 vol% HNO3/4 vol% HF at 140°F (60°C) for 5 min, washed in distilled water and hot-air dried. Teflon/steel interface painted with alkyd varnish before polarization to prevent crevice interference.
alloy.microstructure: Austenitic stainless steel with <1% δ-ferrite. No sigma phase detected by XRD in the experimental alloys.

test_solution.preparation: Aerated; made from reagent-grade chemicals and distilled water.

test_method.procedure_description: Forward anodic polarization in aerated 3.5 wt% NaCl at 25°C with saturated calomel reference; Figure 2 specifies 0.6 V/h. Table 3 repeats Ec from the cyclic measurements; sweep reversal for that table is at 10 mA/cm². Ec is retained independently of reverse-scan Ep.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Clear passive-breakdown potential Ec marking onset of pit initiation; no additional numerical onset-current threshold is specified.

experiments.result_note: Ec denotes the forward-scan critical breakdown / pit-initiation potential, distinct from repassivation Ep. Table 3 repeats the same Ec results. Figure 1 shows sensitized micrographs (620°C/24 h), whereas electrochemical specimens are explicitly machined from annealed stock. That sensitization treatment is not assigned to these tests. AISI 304 Cu, Mo and N entries printed ND remain null; immersion-test pH 0.9 is not the NaCl polarization pH.
